Tiny tan segmented antlion larva with paired curved jaws crawls across a shallow patch of loose sand beside a root; close ground-level side view, morning dappled light. Preserve small body and short legs; no wings.

Small larva sits at the bottom of a deep steep conical sand pit, excavating a little spray of sand; high oblique overhead view emphasizes funnel and tiny occupant, dry grass around rim, late morning. No wings.

Larger plump tan segmented larva waits alert within a wider sand bowl, its paired jaws and dark bead eyes clear; low view from opposite side across pit rim, afternoon shade. Substantially larger body than second stage, no wings.

Intact brown oval cocoon made of many knobbly sand grains rests nestled in sheltered sandy soil beneath a tiny root arch; intimate cross-sectional ground view, warm dusk. Preserve closed seedlike texture, no face or appendages invented.

Open sandy oval cocoon showing golden segmented pupa inside, same form as canonical sprite; sheltered under small dry leaf with shaft of dawn sunlight, three-quarter closeup from the other side. Pupa remains wingless and enclosed, no adult outside.

Fresh brown adult antlion with delicate long transparent veined wings folded along body rests at sandy emergence site, fine clubbed antennae and six legs; low profile facing left, first morning sun, small grasses and abandoned cocoon behind.

Mature slender brown antlion flies across golden meadow with four transparent veined wings spread, dark eyes and two clubbed antennae; diagonal upward flight toward right, broad airy space and distant flowering grasses, sunset.

Older dark brown adult antlion with visibly worn frayed wing edges per canonical sprite settles on a bent grass seedhead looking down over former sandy pits; wings partly open, side view facing left, silver blue evening light, calm dignified aging not death.
